proposals.evidence: DEDR4004 gives Tamil/Malayalam paḻam ripe fruit, Irula pammu/pāmu, Toda pum, Kannada paṇṇu, Parji pal, Gondi paṇḍ(i) and Konda paṇḍu. Selected survey paḷam/payam/pagam/paśam/pām- responses preserve lect-specific reflexes or loss of the medial retroflex, and Kannada/related annu reflects loss of initial h-. These are comparative family proposals; the separate Indo-Aryan-looking phal forms and opaque responses are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4753 gives Tamil maḻai, Malayalam maḻa, Kannada maḻe, Kodagu/Tulu maḷe, Kota may and Toda maw rain. These selected southern survey forms preserve lect-specific lateral, glide, velar or sibilant reflexes and contractions of the rain stem. Minority-lect assignments are comparative extensions; ambiguous source fragments and Indo-Aryan-looking varṣa forms are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4240 gives Tamil pukai, Malayalam puka, Kannada/Kodagu poge, Tulu pugè/pogè, Telugu poga and Gondi poya/poyo/poī smoke. Selected survey p-/h-/zero-initial and intervocalic k/g/h/y forms preserve that family; voga/voge have a glide onset following initial-consonant loss. Source vowel and consonant notation is retained, while opaque longer responses are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR1124 gives Tamil kaṭi, Malayalam kaṭikka and Kannada kaḍi bite. Survey kaḍi/kaḍikkuga preserves the documented southern bite verb with ordinary infinitival endings and source voicing; the unrelated cut entry d1125 is not substituted. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR1931 gives Tamil cem-/civa- red with past -nt-, Malayalam cem-/covva/cuvappu/cōppu red, and Kannada kempu. These selected southern covatta/cuvanda/cem-/cemappu-type survey responses preserve the documented colour family with lect vowels, nasal/labial developments and ordinary adjective endings. Kannada c-initial loan-looking forms are excluded from this group. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
